text:
julia: Uploaded a heatmap for GPU commitments by region and commit type — want quick ops input before we lock renewals Friday EOB. High-level: us-west steady at ~92% util, eu-west trending up (70->86% last 90d), ap-southeast is very bursty (30% avg w/ spikes). Link to sheet: https://redwood.internal/sheets/gpu-commit-heatmap

sam: quick question — is that 92% util measured against reserved vCPU/GPU hours or active GPU pods? can we get committed hours vs effective used hours?

cost-bot: snapshot: 30d rolling: total committed GPU hours = 1,780,000h; used hours = 1,420,000h; utilization = 79.8%; top 3 regions by idle hours: ap-southeast (98k idle), eu-west (45k idle), us-east (31k idle).

ankur: thanks — most of the ap-southeast idle hours are during UTC daytime. That's our dev/test clusters that never got autoscale policies tightened after the last expansion.

maria: do we have any commitments that are in the last month of term where conversion to convertible SPs would help?

leo: yes — two large 3yr reserved blocks in eu-west expire in 42 and 60 days. There's also a 1yr convertible in us-west that matures in 28 days.

julia: action items I'm thinking: (1) tighten autoscale policies for ap-southeast test pools (immediate), (2) consider not renewing the older eu-west 3yr as-is — maybe convert to smaller convertible commitments to handle trend, (3) re-evaluate us-west 1yr convertible and potentially roll into a variable savings plan if our steady load continues. Thoughts?

sam: +1 on tightening autoscale. For renewals, we should run a 90-day forward utilization forecast and compute break-even for 1yr vs 3yr vs SP. I can run the forecast if someone confirms which instance families (A100 vs A10G) to include.

ankur: include both families but weight A100 higher for serving pools. Also factor in a 12% expected demand increase in EU from product launch (internal PRD linked in sheet).

maria: if we switch to more convertible/variable commitments we lose some discount vs fixed, but we get flexibility to reallocate across families and regions. Given the EU trending, I'm leaning convertible for those expiring 3yrs.

leo: question: can we programmatically fall back to on-demand in a region if conversion mispredicts demand? i.e., rollback plan that keeps latency SLOs.

julia: yes — we have capacity routing in the control plane. Fallback to dedicated-host pool in us-west or cross-region failover to eu-west with a small latency penalty. Need to quantify cost delta though.

sam: I'll run two scenarios tonight: 1) renew both eu-west 3yr blocks as 3yr fixed, 2) convert one to convertible + move 20% of load to us-west on high demand. Will attach numbers.

cost-bot: query commands (examples) that we used: ```aws ce get-reservation-purchase-recommendation --service "AmazonEC2" --lookback-period "PAST_30_DAYS"``` and ```gcloud billing budgets list --format=json``` — run with CI creds.

ankur: small ops note — before we convert/shift, please tag any test clusters in ap-southeast with `commit-skip=true` so the billing export excludes leftover test reservations during analysis.

maria: i'm flagging finance: @sam can you add the forecast output + recommended renewal choice to the renewals doc? They'll need 48hr lead for PO if we go fixed.

leo: if eu trend keeps going up we might want extra 6-12 month burstable buffer in dedicated for critical models. That'd be cheaper than overcommitting 3yrs.

julia: agreed. Let's reconvene tomorrow 10am PT. Sam, please post the forecast and decision matrix by 8am so finance/pm can review. I'll take lead on implementing the autoscale tighten in ap-southeast this afternoon and will post a short runbook. :white_check_mark:

sam: on it. I'll include sensitivity to +/−20% demand and show payback windows for 1yr vs 3yr fixed vs convertible.

julia: thanks everyone. If anything urgent pops up, drop in #oncall.

cost-bot: ticket created: CM-4521 "Commitment renewal analysis - eu/us" assigned to sam, due 1765165300.
